variable_description: The position the post takes on the Main Street bike lane proposal.
definition: The post favors the proposal or argues for building the lanes.
examples: Please pass this. | Build the lanes.

definition: The post is against the proposal or argues it should not go ahead as planned.
examples: What a waste of $2 million. | This will kill my restaurant.

definition: The post takes no position, only shares information or asks a question, or its position cannot be determined.
examples: The council votes Thursday at 6pm. | Not sure how I feel about this one yet.

variable_description: The main consideration the post uses to talk about the proposal. Choose the one that gets the most emphasis.
definition: Injuries, deaths, crashes, speeding, emergency access, or feeling safe on the street.
examples: Two cyclists were killed on Main Street in five years.

definition: Business revenue, parking for customers, costs, taxes, property values, or household budgets.
examples: Shops on streets with bike lanes see more foot traffic.

definition: Climate, emissions, air quality, noise, or public health effects of traffic.
examples: Fewer cars downtown means cleaner air.

definition: Who was consulted, who benefits or is left out, accessibility, or how the decision was made.
examples: They held ONE public meeting, at 2pm on a weekday.

definition: None of the frames above is emphasized, including purely informational posts and general praise or dislike.
examples: Does anyone know if the lanes will connect to the river trail?

variable_description: Whether the post attacks or demeans people. Strong disagreement with an idea is not incivility.
definition: Name-calling, insults, or demeaning language aimed at a person or group.
examples: Anyone who thinks this is a good idea is a complete idiot.

definition: No insults or demeaning language aimed at people, even if the tone is angry or sarcastic.
examples: Hard no. Main Street is for cars.
